sources: Puopolo/AAP COFN EOS frameworks — ≥34–35 wk models; ill neonate → cultures/abx without delay; well low-risk → observation pathways
Shane et al. Lancet 2017 — LOS typically >72 h; nonspecific signs; cultures + empiric abx when high suspicion
Bell 1978 / Walsh–Kliegman modified staging — I suspected (hold feeds/observe), II definite medical NEC, III advanced ± perforation (surgery/drain)
Goldstein 2005 — ≥2 age-adjusted SIRS criteria with temp or leukocyte abnormality; legacy vs Phoenix organ-dysfunction definitions
Matics & Sanchez-Pinto 2017 — pSOFA mortality discrimination; optimal cutoff often >7–8; educational domain bins only
Schlapbach et al. JAMA 2024 — infection + Phoenix score ≥2 (resp/CV/coag/neuro); septic shock = sepsis + CV dysfunction
AHA 2020 PALS — rate 100–120/min; infant ~4 cm / child ~5 cm (~⅓ AP); ratios 30:2 single, 15:2 two-rescuer; advanced airway continuous + ~20–30 breaths/min
AHA/PALS IO endorsement; EZ-IO length classes (15/25/45 mm) by weight/tissue depth — educational only
Shukla formulas — UAC/UVC starting depths; radiographic/US tip confirmation before relying on lines
Robinson CRL dating; ACOG first-trimester CRL preferred for EDD (~6 to <14 weeks); redating rules if LMP discrepancy
Phelan AFI method — oligo often AFI <5 cm (or MVP <2 cm); poly often AFI ≥24–25 cm; evaluate ROM, GDM, anomalies
ISUOG Doppler guidance — elevated UA resistance → AEDF → REDF stratifies FGR urgency; AEDF/REDF need specialist inpatient care

issues: nextSteps treated BPP 8–10 as uniformly continue-surveillance; standard interpretation is 8/10 or 10/10 reassuring only with normal amniotic fluid — 8/10 with oligohydramnios is not fully reassuring and needs further evaluation/management.
sources: Manning BPP — 8/10 or 10/10 normal if fluid normal; oligohydramnios warrants further evaluation regardless of composite score
Bishop 1964 — ≤5 often unfavorable (ripening); ≥8 favorable for induction; modifications use length for effacement

issues: nextSteps 'Counsel CS vs OVD' for any arrest incorrectly implies operative vaginal delivery is an option in first-stage arrest; OVD requires complete dilation and is second-stage only.
changes: nextSteps 'Arrest met' action 'Counsel CS vs OVD' → 'Counsel CS (1st stage) or OVD/CS if 2nd stage prerequisites met'
sources: ACOG/SMFM Obstetric Care Consensus No. 1 — active-phase arrest (≥6 cm + ROM + time/UC criteria) → cesarean; second-stage arrest may allow OVD if prerequisites met
ACOG PB 183 — PPH ≥1000 mL or hypovolemia signs; early protocol activation, uterotonics, QBL, escalate MTP/surgical/IR for severe
Obstetric SI — normal often ~0.7–0.9; ≥0.9 concerning; ≥1.0–1.1 higher morbidity/transfusion association
Magpie / ACOG PB 222 — MgSO₄ first-line for eclampsia and severe-feature prophylaxis; stop + calcium gluconate for toxicity
IADPSG 2010 — one-step 75-g OGTT; GDM if any of FPG ≥92, 1-h ≥180, 2-h ≥153 mg/dL
NRP preductal SpO₂ targets — 1 min 60–65% → 10 min 85–95%; MR SOPA/PPV for poor effort/HR; wean excess FiO₂
TTN (delayed fluid clearance, term/late preterm, C-section) vs RDS (surfactant deficiency, preterm); still exclude pneumonia/PPHN
NASPGHAN cholestasis — conjugated hyperbilirubinemia pathologic; early BA workup/referral; fractionate, stool color, ill-infant sepsis/coags
Cappellini Lancet 2008 — X-linked enzymopathy; severe neonatal jaundice and oxidant hemolysis; assay + trigger avoidance
Marshall 1987 PFAPA — clockwork sterile fevers + A/P/A features, well between; steroid abort; exclude cyclic neutropenia/monogenic disease
Ozen EULAR/PRINTO/PRES 2010 — purpura (usually lower limb) + ≥1 of abdominal, joint, renal, or IgA histology; UA/BP follow-up; intussusception caution
